sources.title: About Dream Photonics
sources.locator: About Us narrative, locations and timeline
sources.summary: Dream Photonics identifies itself as a UBC spin-off founded by Lukas Chrostowski and Sudip Shekhar, describes Vancouver and Woodinville operations, and records PDK, packaging, HATCH, FABrIC and customer milestones.

sources.title: Hybrid integration and photonic wire bonding
sources.summary: The company offers chip-to-fibre, laser-to-chip, chip-to-chip and related hybrid integration using free-form polymer structures made by two-photon polymerization.

sources.title: Facet-attached microlenses
sources.summary: Dream Photonics publishes first-party insertion-loss, bandwidth, polarization, power-handling, reflow and environmental-stress claims for 3D-printed facet-attached microlenses.

sources.title: Process design kits
sources.summary: Dream Photonics describes variability-aware and lithography-aware silicon-photonics models, Verilog-A and compact models, SiEPIC deployment, and AIM silicon, silicon-nitride and AMF PWB libraries.

sources.title: FaML-Test-Station-V1 specification and quotation
sources.locator: Product, annual service scope, interfaces and price
sources.summary: The priced USD 25,000 annual offer includes a portable 1550-nm test station and up to ten customer chips with sixteen lenses each, while providing no delivery or subscriber evidence.

sources.title: Contact Dream Photonics
sources.locator: Public contact form and inquiry categories
sources.summary: The official contact page provides a general inquiry path with PWB, PDK, IP and other inquiry categories.

sources.title: Optical Packaging Technician posting
sources.locator: About Us, process equipment and contact
sources.summary: The Vancouver posting describes optical packaging assemblies, process equipment and access to the UBC QMI SONATA 1000, and publishes info@dreamphotonics.com without establishing equipment ownership or production capacity.

sources.title: Dream Photonics component library
sources.locator: Current library version and component table
sources.summary: AIM Photonics lists a current Dream Photonics hardware-verified component library, version 5.5, across its MPW service environment; separate licence agreements may be required for commercialization.

sources.title: NanoSOI photonic wire-bond and microlens option
sources.summary: Applied Nanotools independently lists Dream Photonics facet-attached microlenses and photonic wire bonding as orderable NanoSOI integration options.

sources.title: Reflow-compatible facet-attached microlenses
sources.summary: Dream Photonics and UBC authors report less than one decibel fibre-chip insertion loss on test structures and adaptive correction of alignment offsets, supporting laboratory demonstration rather than volume qualification.

sources.title: Accelerating commercialization of AI and quantum technologies in British Columbia
sources.summary: PacifiCan announced C$1,168,908 for equipment, hiring and a domestic pilot manufacturing facility for optical interconnects used in AI and quantum chips.

sources.title: PacifiCan agreement PC0011803
sources.summary: Open Government records C$1,168,908 from 2026-03-23 to 2029-03-31 to scale manufacturing in British Columbia of quantum light sources for commercial applications.

sources.title: NRC IRAP agreement 1040304
sources.summary: Open Government records C$75,000 from 2026-03-01 to 2026-07-31 to develop facet-attached microlenses for a platform adding optical amplification to silicon-photonic chips.

sources.title: NRC CSTIP agreement 1025699
sources.summary: Open Government records C$1,049,850 from 2025-01-01 to 2028-03-31 for passively aligned packaged III-V single-photon light sources, with Dream Photonics leading commercialization.

sources.title: NRC IRAP agreement 1010973
sources.summary: Open Government records C$500,000 from 2023-09-01 to 2026-03-31 for high-voltage, low-loss integrated photonic switches for cryogenic optical quantum technologies.

sources.title: NRC IRAP agreement 1012199
sources.summary: Open Government records C$50,000 from 2023-11-01 to 2024-03-31 to develop a process design kit and component library for silicon-photonic circuits.

sources.title: NRC announces Canada-UK quantum collaborations
sources.locator: Dream Photonics, Qontrol and Duality project row
sources.summary: NRC identifies Dream Photonics with Qontrol and Duality Quantum Photonics on the H3Lo-QP project for cryogenic integrated photonic switching.

sources.title: 2026 New Ventures BC Competition Top 10 finalists
sources.summary: New Ventures BC named Dream Photonics among ten 2026 competition finalists and scheduled winners for September 21; finalist status is not a prize or technical validation.

sources.title: Top 25 spotlight: Dream Photonics
sources.locator: PICTOR profile, milestones and future targets
sources.summary: The program profile describes PICTOR adaptive micro-optics and a transition from engineering services toward pilot production, while clearly framing customer-part loss, Telcordia qualification, print-speed and paid pilot milestones as future work.

sources.title: PICTOR trademark application 2467657
sources.summary: CIPO records a live, formalized Dream Photonics application for PICTOR awaiting examination; the filing supports use of the name but not registration, allowance or technical performance.

sources.title: BC corporate registry notice for Dream Photonics Inc.
sources.summary: The registry notice records Dream Photonics Inc. as corporation 1232835 incorporated in British Columbia on 2019-12-06; it does not disclose current ownership or good standing.

sources.title: Dream Photonics LINC3D project
sources.summary: FABrIC records C$322,000 for LINC3D to develop wafer-scale 3D-printed optical packaging that integrates fibres and lasers with silicon photonic circuits.

sources.title: Innovative Solutions Canada testing stream
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.summary: The government testing-stream page lists Dream Photonics proposal T11-21914 for 3D-printed microlenses as available for testing, meaning it remains unmatched and does not establish a test, purchase, customer or deployment.

sources.title: UBC Applied Science research report 2023
sources.summary: The UBC report describes Dream Photonics as founded in 2020 by Lukas Chrostowski and Sudip Shekhar, conflicting with the 2019 BC incorporation date as a public founding-year basis.
